subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider `api_error: Internal server error` failures be classified for cron/fallback fast-fail and auth-profile cooldown behavior?
rationale: Mapping the same provider outage text to `server_error`, `timeout`, or `overloaded` changes whether cron retries, whether fallback stops early, and whether auth-profile health is cooled down or left untouched.

options.title: Treat as transient server_error
options.body: Map plain provider internal-server text to a retryable server-outage reason for cron visibility/backoff without poisoning shared auth-profile health unless a narrower provider rule says otherwise.

options.title: Treat as overloaded cooldown
options.body: Adopt the #45625 shape and cool down affected provider/profile routes so fallback skips repeated same-provider failures faster.

options.title: Defer to broader guardrail issue
options.body: Leave #45494 open under the wider reason-aware cron guardrail work and avoid changing provider classification until the full policy matrix is decided.

recommendation.title: Treat as transient server_error
recommendation.body: Map plain provider internal-server text to a retryable server-outage reason for cron visibility/backoff without poisoning shared auth-profile health unless a narrower provider rule says otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the current failover classifier, auth-profile policy, and cron timer surfaces where recent current-main history points to this owner trail.
